Verified Beauty Providers connects customers, service providers, and training providers — with verification as the product's whole premise. My work translates the real Figma system into a live, token-accurate prototype.

verifiedbeautyproviders.com
01The Brief

A directory that had to earn trust, not just claim it.

Before this design, the hub only had a placeholder screen. This became the first real product built from the actual Figma system — "The UK's leading verified Beauty, Wellness & Training directory." Verification isn't a badge bolted onto the UI here; it's the whole reason the product exists, which meant every screen had to carry that promise consistently, not just the homepage.

△

Problem

A three-sided marketplace — customers, service providers, training providers — with 48 distinct screens across discovery, booking, and account management. Nothing had been built yet beyond a "waiting on Figma" placeholder.

◇

Approach

Build directly from the real Figma design, section by section, using the existing token layer rather than inventing new values — and be transparent whenever the source design itself was incomplete, rather than quietly filling gaps.

02Users & Personas

One system, three audiences.

Each role gets its own entry points and its own support content — including three separate Help Centers, one per audience, instead of a single generic FAQ.

PERSONA 01

The Customer

Goals
  • Find a provider or course she can trust quickly
  • Book without back-and-forth phone calls
  • Track rewards and offers across visits
Needs from the product
  • Clear ratings, reviews, and accreditation up front
  • Transparent pricing and flexible cancellation
  • One place for bookings, payments, and rewards
PERSONA 02

The Service Provider

Goals
  • Get discovered by the right customers
  • Prove credentials clearly, not just claim them
  • Fill the calendar without manual admin
Needs from the product
  • A rich profile — team, accreditations, amenities, portfolio
  • Review visibility tied directly to bookings
  • A support channel built for their side of the business
PERSONA 03

The Training Provider

Goals
  • List courses credibly, on equal footing with service providers
  • Manage enrollment and payments without a separate system
  • Build reputation through reviews over time
Needs from the product
  • A distinct course detail and booking/checkout path
  • Not to feel bolted onto the service-provider flow
  • A Help Center written for their specific workflow
⚑ These are target user profiles inferred directly from the product's own three-sided structure and feature set — not backed by user interviews or usability testing, since primary research wasn't part of this project's scope. Framed this way deliberately, rather than presenting them as research that didn't happen.
03User Flows

Two booking journeys, one visual language.

Services and courses are structurally different products — one is scheduled time with a provider, the other is enrollment in a program — so each gets its own flow. Both share the same screen patterns, so switching between them never feels like switching apps.

04The Trust System

Verification that repeats, not a single badge.

Ratings, review counts, and offer badges appear on listing cards before a user opens a detail page. Detail pages add accreditation logos, team credentials, and an amenities grid. Accessibility sits as a first-class filter on the main listing page — wheelchair accessible, women-only, LGBTQ+ friendly — not buried in an "advanced" toggle.

Ratings & reviewsAccreditationAccessibility filtersOffer badgesTeam credentials

★Ratings & Reviews

A 1–5 star score plus review count on every listing card, with a full breakdown and individual reviews on the detail page — the first trust signal a customer sees, before any other detail loads.

✓Accreditation Badges

Verified-provider marks and accreditation logos surfaced on the detail page's Company Profile section — the specifics behind the "verified" claim, not just a green checkmark.

♿Accessibility Filters

Wheelchair accessible, women-only, and LGBTQ+ friendly sit as primary filter checkboxes on the listing page — alongside service type and location, not hidden in an "advanced" panel.

%Offer Badges

Active discounts and "book X, save Y%" offers shown directly on listing cards and reiterated on the detail page — visible before a customer commits to opening a profile.

/beauty-providers/aesthetics
Listing Page — service/treatment, location, rating, offers, and accessibility filters
05Provider Detail

Where the badge becomes specifics.

Everything a customer needs to convert trust into a booking decision, on one screen — no second page required to answer "can I trust this place."

🏷Offers & Pricing

Current offers pinned near the top, followed by a full service menu with per-treatment pricing — no "contact for pricing" dead ends.

🖼Portfolio ("Our Work")

A gallery of past work photos, giving visual proof to sit alongside the written credentials.

👥Meet the Team

Named staff bios with roles and credentials — trust attached to real people, not just the business.

🏆Company Profile & Awards

Accreditations and awards displayed as their own section, plus an amenities icon grid (parking, wheelchair access, and similar) and a location map.

/beauty-providers/elysian-aesthetics-clinic
Service Detail Page — offers, pricing, portfolio, reviews, team, accreditations, amenities
06Retention & Account

A rewards system, not a bolt-on.

Verified Beauty Points (a persistent site-wide banner), Loyalty Points, E-Gift Cards, and Invite-a-Friend referrals — all reachable from one dashboard hub, alongside bookings, wishlist, and payment history. Post-booking states are designed too: rescheduling and cancellation each get their own screen, with a reason captured on cancel.

Loyalty pointsE-gift cardsReferralsReschedule flowCancellation reason

◈Loyalty Points

Points accrue per booking and are tracked in a dedicated dashboard module, redeemable against future bookings — surfaced as a persistent banner sitewide, not just buried in account settings.

🎁E-Gift Cards

Buy, send, or redeem gift cards for yourself or someone else, managed from the same dashboard as loyalty points — reinforcing the same reward loop rather than a separate feature.

👋Invite a Friend

A referral code shareable from the dashboard, with rewards on both sides when a friend joins.

↻Reschedule & Cancellation

Rescheduling has its own "Consider Rescheduling" prompt before a cancellation is finalized, and cancellation itself captures a reason rather than silently deleting the booking.

Also part of the account layer: Profile Management, Payment Methods, Payment History, and a Wishlist for saving services or courses for later — plus three separate, role-specific Help Centers (Customers, Service Providers, Training Providers) instead of one generic FAQ.
/account
User Dashboard — profile, bookings, wishlist, payments, loyalty, gift cards, referrals
07Build Process

Fidelity over shortcuts.

The harder discipline wasn't the visual design — it was resisting the urge to "fix" or invent where the Figma source was incomplete, while still catching and documenting real inconsistencies in the system.

Token reconciliation, not reinvention

Every color on the landing page (primary/500, secondary/100, neutral/1000) mapped exactly onto the existing design tokens — confirmed before writing a line of CSS.

Caught an inconsistency, flagged it

The landing page's real button component uses square corners — diverging from the pill-shaped button built earlier from the style guide. Documented as a gap to reconcile, not silently overridden.

Faithful to incomplete source content

Where Figma's own components still used one repeated placeholder, the build reproduced that faithfully instead of fabricating distinct copy that was never actually specified.

Verified before trusting the tool

A metadata read initially showed two sections as empty. Turned out to be a tooling quirk, not missing content — caught by cross-checking with a full context pull before skipping anything.

08Design System

Typography & color, pulled from source.

Headings in Advice Medium Lys, body and UI text in Montserrat. The palette below is the real token layer — not approximated, pulled directly from the Figma style guide's variable definitions.

09Status

Where it stands today.

This is a live, in-progress build, not a finished shipped product — and that's the honest framing at this stage. The value on display is process rigor on a system large enough that shortcuts would be easy to take and hard to notice.
